evidence: Exempt by DERIVATION, not merely by basis. data/wesselmann_2018_ostracism_veterans.py melts the PLOS S1 .sav on the literal column list [f'social{i}' for i in range(1,16)] (var_name='item'), so the IRW item code IS the source column name (pattern 1: no rename, no positional assignment): 15/15 live item codes present verbatim in the .sav header, 15/15 carrying their own SPSS variable label (lengths 57-100 chars, all far under the 255 truncation cap), and item_text equals those labels with 15/15 exact string equality. Corroborated independently by the authors' OSF codebook (sha256 b3e1ee71...8a9c), 15/15 identical after collapsing PDF line wrapping. No positional step exists that could permute text across codes. The resp AXIS did carry inference (the .sav has 0 value-label sets and the codebook misprints anchor 1 as 'Strongly Agree') and was checked numerically, N=128: social6R/social8R equal 6-social6/6-social8 with max |diff| = 0.0, and the file's own 'support' composite equals mean(social1-5, social6R, social7, social8R, social9-15) with max |diff| = 0.000 vs 0.533 for the plain raw mean, so the IRW table stores social6/social8 unreversed; that composite correlates -0.511 ptsd, -0.461 traitanx, -0.532 distress, -0.550 chronic ostracism, +0.594 basicneeds, +0.596 milsupport, fixing 1 = 'Strongly Disagree' and 5 = 'Strongly Agree'. The -0.550 reproduces the paper's reported civilian-support x ostracism r = -.55 and keyed alpha 0.902 (n=124) reproduces the paper's .90. What this does NOT establish: nothing tests the three interior anchors 'Somewhat Disagree' / 'Neither Agree nor Disagree' / 'Somewhat Agree' individually -- they are the codebook's own printed labels for 2/3/4; only the endpoints and the monotone direction are checked.
